title: Declared decimal scale and beyond-double precision are destroyed before the flattener ever runs
rationale: On the JSON stack neither half of the BigDecimal story applies: JsonFlattener sets USE_BIG_DECIMAL_FOR_FLOATS to false, so every JSON fraction becomes a Double at PARSE time and MapFlattener never sees a BigDecimal. The loss is earlier, unconditional, and not mentioned anywhere in the library documentation of the issue.
catchesBugClass: Any claim of lossless round-tripping for monetary or fixed-scale data on the JSON path; a mapper reconfiguration that changes float handling in either direction.
cannotCatch: Cannot be observed on the MAP stack at all - the harness builds sourceMap with the same Jackson, so the Double is already lossy before flatten() is called. It also cannot show what a fix would cost.

predicted.detail: Declared scale is gone on trailingZero and oneFive; highScale drops to double precision; beyondDouble becomes indistinguishable from the literal 1.0. The exact digit strings are Jackson/JDK details - if measurement differs, correct the literal, not the classification.
